title: Opposite coherence for join-slice and comma-cone comparisons
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor objects and coherent comma cones from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial set $K$ define $K^{\mathrm{op}}_m=K_m$ with the operator of $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$ given by the operator of $\alpha^\vee(i)=m-\alpha(r-i)$ on $K$. For a simplicial map $f$, $f^{\mathrm{op}}$ has the same degreewise components. Let $Y$ be a small simplicial set, $C$ a quasicategory and $d:Y\to C$ a diagram. Put $Q=C_{/d}$ with its left join-slice construction from [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], and $V=(\Delta_Y\downarrow d)$ with its coherent comma construction. Put $a=d^{\mathrm{op}}:Y^{\mathrm{op}}\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Then $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory, and the right join slice $J_a$, coherent cocone category $P_a$ and fat-join comparison $r_a:J_a\to P_a$ are those of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison]. There are natural simplicial isomorphisms over $C^{\mathrm{op}}$
$$R:Q^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{\cong}J_a,\qquad S:V^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{\cong}P_a.$$
In degree $m$, $R$ takes $H:\Delta^m\star Y\to C$ to $H^{\mathrm{op}}$ precomposed with the ordered-block reversal $Y^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^m\cong(\Delta^m\star Y)^{\mathrm{op}}$; the parameter simplex is identified with $(\Delta^m)^{\mathrm{op}}$ by $i\mapsto m-i$. For $S$, represent a comma simplex by an apex map $x:\Delta^m\to C$ and a map $h:Y\times\Delta^m\times\Delta^1\to C$ with $h(y,t,0)=x(t)$ and $h(y,t,1)=d(y)$. Its image is obtained by taking opposites, reversing the parameter simplex and the interval, so that the resulting cocone starts at $a$ and ends at the constant diagram at the reversed apex. Both isomorphisms commute with all simplex operators and with restriction in $Y$ and postcomposition in $C$.

These isomorphisms identify the specified comparison cones, not just their apices. Explicitly, for every vertex $\ell:\Delta^0\star Y\to C$ of $Q$, the vertex $S_0^{-1}(r_{a,0}(R_0(\ell)))$ of $V$ is exactly $\ell$ precomposed with the fat left-cone collapse
$$T_Y=\Delta^0\amalg_{Y\times\{0\}}(Y\times\Delta^1)\longrightarrow\Delta^0\star Y$$
of [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]. Here the equality is under the defining equality of the degree-zero sets of a simplicial set and its opposite. It fixes the entire boundary diagram and the cone vertex. All assertions allow $Y=\varnothing$.

source.place: Riehl–Verity, Definition 2.1.14 (simplicial opposite), Definitions 3.2.4–3.2.5 and Example 3.2.6 (join/comma cones), and the cone in (6.1.1), published pp. 680, 684–685 and 707. Agent refinement: explicit opposite isomorphisms and compatibility with the prescribed fat-join comparison of the existing DAG nodes. Author-hosted PDF read in the retained sandbox; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this simplicial comparison.

proof.text:
Write $\alpha^\vee(i)=m-\alpha(r-i)$ for $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$. Direct substitution gives $(\alpha\beta)^\vee=\alpha^\vee\beta^\vee$ and $(\alpha^\vee)^\vee=\alpha$, so the opposite construction in the statement is simplicial and involutive, on maps as well as objects. Define $\rho_m:\Delta^m\to(\Delta^m)^{\mathrm{op}}$ on a $k$-simplex $\beta:[k]\to[m]$ by $\beta\mapsto\beta^\vee$. The equation $(\beta\gamma)^\vee=\beta^\vee\gamma^\vee$ proves simpliciality, and double reversal supplies its inverse. For $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$ it also gives
$$\rho_m\Delta(\alpha)=(\Delta(\alpha^\vee))^{\mathrm{op}}\rho_r.$$
Opposites preserve degreewise products: both product operators apply the same reversed operator to each coordinate.

source.place: Definition 2.1.14, published p.680; agent expansion of the order-reversal definition.

proof.text: The horn description in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] says a simplex lies in $\Lambda_i^n$ precisely when its image misses a vertex different from $i$. Reversing vertex indices therefore identifies $(\Lambda_i^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ with $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$ under $\rho_n$. For $0<i<n$, a horn in $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ reverses to this inner horn in $C$, has a filler by the quasicategory hypothesis, and reversing that filler fills the original horn. Thus $C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory. The opposite $Y^{\mathrm{op}}$ is still small, because its sets of simplices are unchanged. Apply [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] to $L=Y^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\mathcal E=C^{\mathrm{op}}$, $a=d^{\mathrm{op}}$. It supplies exactly the specified $J_a$, $P_a$ and comparison $r_a$, defined by precomposition with the fat-join collapse, and makes the two targets quasicategories.

source.place: Definition 2.1.14 and Example 3.2.6, published pp.680,685; horn calculation and application of the existing comparison theorem.

proof.text:
For each $m$ define
$$b_m:Y^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^m\longrightarrow(\Delta^m\star Y)^{\mathrm{op}}.$$
On the pure $Y$ summand it is the identity, on the pure parameter summand it is $\rho_m$, and on a mixed $k$-simplex $(y,\beta)$ with $y\in Y_v$, $\beta:[u]\to[m]$, $u+v+1=k$, it sends $(y,\beta)$ to $(\beta^\vee,y)$ in the underlying $\Delta^m_u\times Y_v$ summand. These formulas reverse the order of the two blocks. To check an operator $\gamma:[h]\to[k]$, split its ordered image into the part in each block, allowing one part to be empty. The reversed operator $\gamma^\vee$ selects those same two parts in the reverse order and reverses the restricted maps within them. The $Y^{\mathrm{op}}$ operator is exactly this reversed restriction; for the parameter it agrees by $(\beta\delta)^\vee=\beta^\vee\delta^\vee$. The same check with an empty part gives the pure cases. Hence $b_m$ is simplicial. Swapping the blocks back and reversing $\beta$ again is an inverse, since $(\beta^\vee)^\vee=\beta$.

source.place: Example 3.2.6 and the join cone in (6.1.1), published pp.685,707; explicit calculation using the existing degreewise join formula.

proof.text:
For $H\in Q_m$ put $R_m(H)=H^{\mathrm{op}}b_m$. It restricts on $Y^{\mathrm{op}}$ to $a$, so belongs to $(J_a)_m$. Its apex is $(H|_{\Delta^m})^{\mathrm{op}}\rho_m$; a map $x:\Delta^m\to C$ represents the element $x_m(\mathrm{id}_{[m]})\in C_m$, and this reversed apex represents the identical element in $(C^{\mathrm{op}})_m$, because $\rho_m$ fixes the identity simplex. Thus $R$ is over $C^{\mathrm{op}}$. The formulas for $b$ give
$$b_m(\mathrm{id}\star\Delta(\alpha))=(\Delta(\alpha^\vee)\star\mathrm{id})^{\mathrm{op}}b_r.$$
The $\alpha$-operator in $Q^{\mathrm{op}}$ sends $H$ to $H(\Delta(\alpha^\vee)\star\mathrm{id})$, whereas in $J_a$ it is restriction along $\mathrm{id}\star\Delta(\alpha)$. The displayed equality therefore proves that $R$ commutes with every operator. Each $R_m$ is bijective: apply opposite and $b_m^{-1}$ to recover $H$. These inverses commute with operators by the same equality. This proves the stated simplicial isomorphism $R$.

source.place: Definition 2.1.14, Example 3.2.6 and (6.1.1); agent verification of the join-slice reversal in every parameter degree.

proof.text:
Uncurry the defining comma pullback in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Its $m$-simplices are exactly $(x,h)$ with the endpoints in the statement, and operators precompose $x$ and the parameter coordinate of $h$. Define
$$\widetilde x=x^{\mathrm{op}}\rho_m,\qquad
\widetilde h=h^{\mathrm{op}}(\mathrm{id}_{Y^{\mathrm{op}}}\times\rho_m\times\rho_1).$$
Products commute with opposite by Step 1, so these are maps to $C^{\mathrm{op}}$. Since $\rho_1$ interchanges the endpoints, $\widetilde h|_0=a\operatorname{pr}_{Y^{\mathrm{op}}}$ and $\widetilde h|_1=\widetilde x\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^m}$. Currying therefore gives an $m$-simplex of exactly $P_a$, with apex $\widetilde x$. Put $S_m(x,h)=(\widetilde x,\widetilde h)$. On a $k$-simplex $(y,\beta,\epsilon)$ the cylinder formula is
$$\widetilde h_k(y,\beta,\epsilon)=h_k(y,\beta^\vee,\epsilon^\vee).$$
This specifies the entire coherent transformation, including all higher cylinder simplices.

source.place: Definitions 3.2.3–3.2.4, published p.684, and Definition 2.1.14; agent expansion of the comma pullback and reversal formula.

proof.text: For $\alpha:[r]\to[m]$, an operator in $V^{\mathrm{op}}$ restricts the old parameter by $\alpha^\vee$. Step 1 gives $\rho_m\Delta(\alpha)=(\Delta(\alpha^\vee))^{\mathrm{op}}\rho_r$, and the identity on the $Y$ coordinate and $\rho_1$ on the interval do not depend on $m$. Substitution in the formulas of Step 5 therefore proves $S_r(V(\alpha^\vee)(x,h))=P_a(\alpha)S_m(x,h)$. Repeating those formulas, now starting from a cocone in $C^{\mathrm{op}}$, reverses its two endpoints again and gives $(x,h)$: on each coordinate this is $(\beta^\vee)^\vee=\beta$ and $(\epsilon^\vee)^\vee=\epsilon$. It is an inverse in every degree and hence a simplicial inverse. The apex calculation in Step 4 applies also to $\widetilde x$, so $S$ lies over $C^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Definitions 2.1.14 and 3.2.4, published pp.680,684; direct operator and inverse checks for the specified comma objects.

proof.text: Let $f:Y'\to Y$ and restrict $d$ to $df$. On each join summand, applying $f$ to $y$ commutes with $b_m$, because its other coordinate is unchanged and $f$ is simplicial. Thus $R$ commutes with restriction in $Y$. In the formula for $S$, restriction replaces $h_k(y,\beta,\epsilon)$ by $h_k(f_k(y'),\beta,\epsilon)$; this also commutes with reversing $\beta,\epsilon$. For a simplicial map $g:C\to C'$, postcomposition replaces $H_k,h_k,x_k$ by $g_kH_k,g_kh_k,g_kx_k$. Since taking opposite leaves these degreewise functions unchanged, both formulas commute with this postcomposition. The same is true of their inverses. These are strict equalities of simplicial maps and require no choice of equivalences or coherence fillers. When one uses the quasicategorical comparison theorem, the postcomposition target $C'$ is of course a quasicategory.

source.place: Definition 2.1.14 and Definitions 3.2.3–3.2.4; naturality checked on the explicit components.

proof.text: Fix a vertex $\ell:\Delta^0\star Y\to C$ and let $x=\ell|_{\Delta^0}$. Put $k=R_0(\ell)$. By the defining clause of [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison], $r_{a,0}(k)$ has cylinder $k$ precomposed with $Y^{\mathrm{op}}\times\Delta^1\to Y^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^0$: for an $n$-simplex $(y,u)$, the collapse keeps the restriction of $y$ to the initial $0$-block of $u:[n]\to[1]$ and puts the constant apex on its final $1$-block. Applying $S_0^{-1}$ replaces $u$ by $u^\vee(i)=1-u(n-i)$; the parameter $\Delta^0$ stays fixed. The initial $0$-block of $u^\vee$ is exactly the reversed final $1$-block of $u$, and its final $1$-block is the reversed initial $0$-block of $u$. Applying $b_0$ to the collapsed simplex therefore puts $x$ on the initial $0$-block of $u$ and the restriction of $y$ on its final $1$-block. In fact, if the latter block starts at $t$, its inclusion $\delta:\{0,\ldots,n-t\}\to[n]$, $j\mapsto t+j$, is the reversal of the initial-block inclusion; the $Y^{\mathrm{op}}$ restriction becomes exactly $Y(\delta)y$. This is precisely the left-cone collapse in [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus]. Pure blocks give respectively the constant apex or $y$. Consequently the resulting cylinder is exactly $\ell$ after that collapse, on every simplex, not merely up to homotopy.

source.place: Example 3.2.6 and (6.1.1), published pp.685,707; agent refinement comparing the prescribed right fat-join and left fat-cone collapses.

proof.text: At $u=0$ the cylinder of Step 8 is constant at $x$, and at $u=1$ it is exactly $d$ on the whole simplicial set $Y$. It therefore descends, with its separately retained apex $x$, to $T_Y=\Delta^0\amalg_{Y\times\{0\}}(Y\times\Delta^1)$, and is $\ell$ precomposed with its prescribed collapse. The degree-zero sets of an object and its opposite are identical, so this proves the literal vertex equality in the statement. No operation above requires a simplex of $Y$. If $Y=\varnothing$, then $Q=C$, $J_a=C^{\mathrm{op}}$, and both comma objects are their apex objects because their cylinder data have empty domain. Both isomorphisms are then the identity under these identifications. The fat joins and $T_Y$ reduce to their apex or parameter simplices, so the same vertex equality holds. If $C$ has no vertices there are no such $\ell$ and that assertion is vacuous; the isomorphisms still hold in every degree.

source.place: Definitions 3.2.3–3.2.4 and (6.1.1); endpoints and empty-shape cases of the explicit constructions.
